transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-12 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Daniel Park (Head of ML - Orionix), Sara Lopez (Platform Eng), Amir Khan (VP Product), Jin Park (SRE)

Summary:
Quick sync to align pilot scope, runway (budget + timeline), and technical tests needed to validate latency and cost targets before a Q3 procurement decision. Agreed on artifacts Redwood will send and traces Orionix will provide. Decided on a short benchmark window and an internal canary plan.

Topics discussed:
- Pilot scope and success metrics (p95 latency < 120ms for single-turn generation, token cost targets)
- Data handling, KMS, and SOC 2 concerns for pilot
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for runway and cost predictability
- Benchmark plan: replay + live spike tests, KV cache warmup
- Rollout timeline and exec sign-off checkpoints

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you carving out time. Quick round of intros?
[00:07] Daniel Park: Daniel here, head of ML for Orionix. We're looking to move our recommendation and safety filtering to a hosted inference stack, and we want to validate latency/cost before committing.
[00:14] Amir Khan: Amir — product, and we'll own sign-off from a business side.
[00:17] Sara Lopez: Sara, platform eng — I'll be point for the trace and infra hooks.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great. Liam — do you want to frame the technical checklist for the pilot?
[00:25] Liam O'Rourke: Yep. So our pilot checklist usually includes three things: representative traffic replay, a live spike test, and an SLA-ish acceptance run. For your targets you mentioned p95 under 120ms, is that for a single-turn short completion?
[00:36] Daniel Park: Correct. Most calls are short — ~40 to 80 tokens.
[00:41] Liam O'Rourke: Cool. We'll want to look at tokenization differences and KV cache warmup because those skew early latency. Also, uh, if you have multi-turn chat-state we need to map how you persist context — are you planning to keep full context on the client?
[00:52] Sara Lopez: We'll pass a 3-turn history in headers, size is bounded. We'll provide sample payloads with the trace.
[00:57] Liam O'Rourke: Perfect. That helps with batching sim.
[01:03] Priya Nair: From the account side, timeline wise — what does everyone think about a two-week benchmark window followed by a 4-week pilot ramp?
[01:10] Amir Khan: Sounds reasonable; finance needs cost estimate up front though.
[01:13] Maya Chen: We'll include a provisional Dedicated estimate and a hosted break-even analysis in the cost sheet.
[01:18] Daniel Park: On security, we need to confirm KMS integration and audit logs. SOC 2 is table stakes for us.
[01:23] Maya Chen: Understood. We will share our SOC 2 attestation and the KMS integration guide. For Private we can provide a VPC option if needed, and our logs support per-request trace IDs.
[01:33] Jin Park: A question on data retention — during the pilot, can logs be set to auto-expire? We can't keep customer prompts longer than 30 days.
[01:38] Liam O'Rourke: Yes, retention is configurable. We'll set pilot retention to 30 days and show you the audit log pipeline.
[01:44] Daniel Park: Good. On the latency front, what are the knobs — batching, quantization, or Dedicated?
[01:49] Liam O'Rourke: All of the above. For low p95 you typically use a Dedicated pool sized to your qps, plus small batch target (we prefer continuous batching to avoid queuing spikes). Quantization helps with throughput and cost but can affect output fidelity; we can A/B that in the pilot.
[02:03] Sara Lopez: When you say quantization, do you mean 8-bit or some mixed scheme? Our safety models are sensitive to even minor distribution shifts.
[02:10] Liam O'Rourke: We typically start with static 8-bit PTQ for throughput, and run alignment checks. If you need fidelity, there's a 16-bit mixed path or alpha quant presets we can test. We'll surface regression metrics.
[02:21] Amir Khan: For procurement we need a clear fallback policy — if Dedicated is unavailable we need auto-fallback to hosted without SLA break.
[02:28] Maya Chen: That's built into our routing policies. We'll outline canary + fallback in the runbook. It can fail open to a lower-tier model if a Dedicated pool drops.
[02:36] Daniel Park: Ok, great. Let's talk about the benchmark specifics — replay rate, spike profile?
[02:40] Liam O'Rourke: We ask for a representative 48-hour trace. We'll run a steady replay at normal qps, then do controlled spikes (2x and 5x) for short bursts, and an end-of-window p95 acceptance pass after KV warmup. Also we'll instrument token-level latency and cost.
[02:56] Sara Lopez: We'll scrub PII and provide the trace by Friday. Expect some formatting oddities — our logs have a few weird headers.
[03:03] Liam O'Rourke: That's fine. We can ingest JSONL, and we'll document the mapping in the runbook.
[03:08] Priya Nair: I'll put the runbook link in the follow-up email, with the cost spreadsheet.
[03:13] Maya Chen: Thanks. One more thing — how are we measuring quality regression during quantization?
[03:18] Liam O'Rourke: We do prompt-set evals, pass/fail on key business prompts, and an automated ROUGE/semantic similarity suite where applicable. We'll also capture hallucination-related flags.
[03:27] Daniel Park: Make sure to include our safety prompts, we care a lot about false positives.
[03:31] Liam O'Rourke: Absolutely. Bring those in the anonymized prompt set.
[03:35] Amir Khan: From a timeline perspective, if we get the trace by Thursday and Redwood runs a quick baseline, can we get results before next Tuesday?
[03:42] Maya Chen: Yes, Liam — doable?
[03:45] Liam O'Rourke: Yeah, we can run an expedited baseline and share a latency/cost summary by Monday EOD, assuming the trace ingestion is smooth. The more the trace matches production shape the less guesswork.
[03:56] Sara Lopez: A lingering question about observability — we want token-level cost breakup in console and per-route latency histograms.
[04:03] Maya Chen: That's in our Console — per-route dashboards and token-level cost. We'll add an Orionix view and give you metrics access for the pilot.
[04:12] Jin Park: Will we get tracing correlation IDs so our SREs can stitch requests end-to-end?
[04:16] Liam O'Rourke: Yes, we propagate trace IDs and you can point to our tracing hooks. We'll share the tracing doc.
[04:21] Daniel Park: Great. I'm hearing readiness, cost, and an exec check. What's the approval gating after the pilot?
[04:27] Priya Nair: Typically pilot success -> SLAs and capacity commitment conversation with Finance and Eng execs. We'll schedule that once the pilot shows we meet p95 and cost targets.
[04:35] Amir Khan: We want a one-pager with break-even analysis for our CFO.
[04:38] Maya Chen: We'll include that in the cost sheet.
[04:41] Sara Lopez: A couple of nitty-gritty items — do you support our SSO provider (Okta) and can we use SAML SCIM for user provisioning?
[04:49] Maya Chen: Yes, SSO via SAML/Okta and SCIM user sync are supported. We'll attach our security integration guide.
[04:56] Daniel Park: Any competitors or gotchas we should watch for on the tech side?
[04:59] Liam O'Rourke: Some teams prototype in-house but hit ops scaling gaps — especially with KV cache management and autoscaling. Anthropic and OpenAI are also referenced in RFIs; we try to be transparent about latency/cost tradeoffs.
[05:14] Amir Khan: Ok, action items recap?
[05:17] Maya Chen: Maya: pilot runbook + cost sheet (target 2026-06-16). Liam: expedited baseline after trace (share by 2026-06-20). Daniel: provide scrubbed 48-hour trace + prompt set (target 2026-06-18). Priya: schedule exec 30-min follow-up post-kickoff (target 2026-06-21).
[05:37] Daniel Park: Sounds good. Any outstanding risks?
[05:40] Jin Park: Risk: our spike profile includes long-tail bursts from batch jobs; we'll mark those in the trace. If those are missed, it skews headroom.
[05:49] Liam O'Rourke: We'll include long-tail microbursts in the test plan.
[05:53] Sara Lopez: Another minor point — we may need an NDA addendum for certain prompt sets.
[05:58] Maya Chen: Noted. I'll have Legal loop in if needed.
[06:02] Amir Khan: Alright, thanks all. Looking forward to the runbook and the baseline numbers.
[06:07] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the links and the spreadsheet.
[06:10] Priya Nair: I'll confirm the exec slot after we see initial results.
[06:14] End of meeting.
